newsitem.title: UK: Reform of Russian oil output sharing seen on track.
newsitem.headline: Reform of Russian oil output sharing seen on track.

text.p: Reform of Russia's controversial Production Sharing Agreement (PSA) legislation in the energy sector is on course for this year, the State Duma's deputy chairman, Artur Chilingarov, told a conference here on Thursday.

"Parliamentarians are at last beginning to understand the PSA law is worth adopting," said Chilingarov. "Many areas are not favourable. Tax levels need further clarification, but at last we're ready to discuss it."
He said that reform is also needed on the law concerning subsurface resources, on customs tariffs and on mortgages.
And he said Russia needs to move towards using the civil law to resolve disputes between foreign and local companies.
"Will we be able to pass a package of laws bearing in mind the huge influence of the communists and agrarians, can we push it through?" he asked. "Realistically, we can hope to."
He added that whoever is in charge of the country, they know that without an attractive fiscal regime they will never be able to develop mineral resources.

Chilingarov later told a press conference that when the initial law went through the Duma, there was a school of thought which said it was an attempt to pillage Russia's resources and would only damage the country. This made the first law a compromise, he added.

"To be effective, it needs a list of fields (to be included under the legislation). We started with 120 fields. I know next week a draft will be given to the Duma, and the list will then have a maximum of 20 fields," he said. "If it goes through it will be another compromise. But I hope it will at least be adopted."
